The test constructs `message.text` as `"alpha beta gamma https://x.y/z omega"` with four entities in order by offset: bold over `"alpha beta gamma"` (offset 0, length 16), italic over `"beta"` (6,4), code over `"gamma"` (11,5), and URL over `"https://x.y/z"` (17,13). The property accessed is `message.text_html_urled`, so `_parse_html(..., urled=True)` is the relevant path, and the URL branch at lines 4674-4675 will be active for URL entities. Reading `_parse_html`, it sorts entities by offset, recursively parses nested entities, and otherwise uses `escape(text)` for leaf entities. For the outer call, the bold entity contains the italic and code entities, so its `escaped_text` comes from a recursive `_parse_html` on `"alpha beta gamma"`, producing `""` and `""` markup inside the bold wrapper. Then the outer loop later reaches the URL entity. That URL entity has no nested entities, so line 4668 sets `escaped_text = escape(text)`. Since the URL text is `"https://x.y/z"` and contains no HTML-special characters that `html.escape` would change, `escaped_text` stays `"https://x.y/z"`. Because the entity type is `MessageEntity.URL` and `urled` is true, line 4675 sets `insert = f'{escaped_text}'`, which becomes `"https://x.y/z"`. To get the final `html_text`, lines 4705-4717 append escaped non-entity text plus each entity insertion in order. The bold entity contributes `"alpha beta gamma"`. Between the bold entity ending at offset 16 and the URL entity starting at 17 there is one plain space, so a space is appended before the URL anchor. After the URL entity ends at offset 30, the remaining plain text is `" omega"`, which is appended escaped unchanged. So the final returned `html_text` is `"alpha beta gamma https://x.y/z omega"`.
